title: Natural comparison of Ext sheaf cohomology with derived global sections
statement: Let X be any scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and q a nonnegative integer. On abelian sheaves on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], the functor F ↦ Sheaf.H F q (Ext from the constant integer sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]) is naturally isomorphic, as an abelian-group-valued functor, to F ↦ H^q(RΓ(X,F[0])) [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No compactness, dimension, reducedness, or torsion assumption is imposed.

source.place: Definition 015A, Lemmas 05TI and 06XR; the injective-resolution convention for cohomology in Etale Cohomology Lemma 03Q5.

proof.text: For the constant integer sheaf Z_X, use constantSheafΓAdj.homAddEquiv followed by uliftZMultiplesAddEquiv to identify Hom(Z_X,F) additively with Γ(F). Compose this with Cochain.fromSingleEquiv in each degree to construct an isomorphism from the Hom complex of Z_X[0] to any sheaf complex K onto the complex Γ(K). The adjunction naturality and δ_fromSingleMk prove compatibility with differentials and with every morphism of complexes. These compatibility proofs are written out as private helpers in the item module.

Choose injectiveResolution F. Its extAddEquivCohomologyClass identifies Sheaf.H F q with the cohomology classes of Hom(Z_X[0],I_F). The explicit leftHomologyData identifies these classes with homology, and the preceding complex isomorphism identifies that homology with H^q(Γ(I_F)). Compose with isoRightDerivedObjCochainComplex.symm to obtain Sheaf.H F q ≅ R^qΓ(F). To prove naturality, define postcomposition on cochains, cocycles and their quotient and verify the associated LeftHomologyMapData. Lift f:F→G by InjectiveResolution.desc. The equality extMk_comp_mk₀, applied to representatives supplied by extMk_surjective, proves compatibility with Ext maps; combine it with the proved homology naturality and isoRightDerivedObjCochainComplex_inv_naturality. NatIso.ofComponents packages the resulting natural isomorphism.

Whisker rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility.symm by the degree-zero single functor and the qth homology functor. Compose with singleFunctorCompRightDerivedFunctorPlusCompHomologyFunctorIso to identify H^q(RΓ(F[0])) naturally with R^qΓ(F). Compose the inverse of this isomorphism with the preceding Sheaf.H comparison. All degrees are handled uniformly, including q=0; no case-split theorem or unresolved comparison lemma is used.
